rows.why: A machine-checked proof shows the sign-twisted incidence operator has full rank on this patch; the premise carries that result over to the model.
rows.statement: The frozen finite local domain of 8662 carriers and 11816 seams, with its declared reversing seam transport and unit-counting measure, on which Lean/OphGap/OphOrigWitness.lean proves the sign-twisted incidence operator has full rank, is a domain of the native process of the executable model.

rows.name: anomalous collar charge as physical gravitating stress
rows.what: Modular charge left on unrecovered overlap collars is a real local stress that gravitates with the same Newton coupling as ordinary matter.
rows.why: It is the dark-matter mechanism: anomalous gravity around galaxies comes from these collars, with placement and density set by one source.
rows.statement: Anomalous modular charge retained on unrecovered overlap collars is a physical local stress that gravitates with the Newton coupling measured on ordinary matter, and the location, density per proper length and per-cut variance per unit baryonic mass of the gravitating collars around galaxies are supplied by one physical source (Premise Collar scale of the dark-sector paper).

rows.name: fixed global record capacity
rows.what: The total record capacity of the universe is positive and constant over the whole range of cosmic expansion compared with data.
rows.why: A constant capacity gives a constant dark-energy density, so the cosmological-constant reading of dark energy relies on it.
rows.statement: The global record capacity N(a) is positive and constant for every scale factor in the scored range.

rows.name: record capacity equals de Sitter horizon entropy
rows.what: The universe's correctable public-record capacity, in nats, equals the entropy of one de Sitter horizon whose area observers measure.
rows.why: It links record capacity to the cosmological constant, letting OPH express dark energy through the size of the record capacity.
rows.statement: The correctable public-record capacity N selected on the refinement family equals, in nats, the entropy A/(4 l*^2) of one de Sitter causal horizon whose area observers measure on the same process.

rows.name: physical primordial source map
rows.what: One finite source in the model emits all data needed to turn screen fluctuations into physical primordial curvature perturbations for standard CMB transfer.
rows.why: Every OPH prediction for the cosmic microwave background spectrum depends on this map from screen covariance to primordial curvature modes.
rows.statement: One finite source on the executable process emits the geometric screen scalar, the primitive collar release law and release energy, the conformal precision on the round sphere, conserved stress, a common clock and release surface, a physical scale and a radial observation map, and these map the screen covariance into physical primordial curvature modes entering standard CMB transfer.

rows.name: collar generator density as the scalar spectral tilt
rows.what: The collar's reserve generator has density P/24, and its source-facing half, P/48, is the survival tilt, equal to 1 - n_s.
rows.why: This value fixes the tilt of the survival cocycle, which OPH reads as the scalar spectral tilt of primordial fluctuations.
rows.statement: The infinitesimal reserve generator of the collar has full-collar density P/24, and the weighted orientation-reversal coarea identity assigns its source-facing half P/48 as the tilt of the survival cocycle.

rows.name: common bulk field behind the screens
rows.what: One homogeneous, isotropic scalar field on a common flat three-dimensional slice restricts, with one normalization, to the observed screens at arbitrarily large radii.
rows.why: It lets screen fluctuations be read as one three-dimensional primordial field, as standard cosmological perturbation analysis requires.
rows.statement: One homogeneous isotropic scalar field on a common Euclidean three-dimensional slice, with locally integrable off-diagonal covariance and no contact terms, restricts in one normalization to the observed screens at an unbounded sequence of radii.

rows.name: physical dilation intertwiner
rows.what: A physical dilation map carries the source survival cocycle, with one fixed exponent, to the curvature covariance of a homogeneous radial source family.
rows.why: It turns the survival tilt into the scale dependence of the primordial power spectrum, which the spectral-index prediction uses.
rows.statement: A physical dilation intertwiner transfers the source survival cocycle with one fixed exponent to the curvature covariance on a homogeneous radial source family, on a common compact log-wavenumber core.

rows.name: zero primordial tensor data
rows.what: Primordial gravitational waves start with zero amplitude and zero velocity, and nothing sources them on the background.
rows.why: It sets the primordial tensor-to-scalar ratio to zero, which polarization searches in the cosmic microwave background can test.
rows.statement: Primordial tensor modes have zero initial amplitude and zero initial velocity and no tensor forcing on the declared background.

rows.name: one common release clock
rows.what: All particle species are released by one Gaussian single-clock source on one common release clock.
rows.why: A single clock makes primordial perturbations adiabatic, with no isocurvature modes, as standard CMB fits assume.
rows.statement: All species are released by a rank-one Gaussian single-clock source on one common release clock.

rows.name: flat clock-slice FLRW identification
rows.what: The cosmic background is a clocked Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker expansion whose spatial slices have zero curvature.
rows.why: Spatial flatness enters every background distance and CMB calculation and fixes the geometry of the cosmological predictions.
rows.statement: The cosmological background is a clocked FLRW continuation whose spatial Levi-Civita connection has vanishing area-normalized small-loop holonomy.

rows.name: horizon-scale coherence of the primordial source
rows.what: The primordial source is correlated over distances larger than the causal horizon of the background at the time of release.
rows.why: It accounts for CMB correlations between regions never in causal contact, the problem inflation is usually invoked to solve.
rows.statement: The primordial source is coherent across scales larger than the causal horizon of the record-density background at release.

rows.name: hot radiation state on a common clock
rows.what: The early universe begins in a hot thermal radiation state of declared particle species, read on one common physical clock.
rows.why: Hot big bang physics, including nucleosynthesis and the cosmic microwave background, starts from this initial state.
rows.statement: The early federation is prepared in a hot thermal radiation state of declared species, read on one common physical clock.

rows.name: source Euclidean slab data for a vacuum
rows.what: The source supplies reversible Euclidean slab data, including conductances, potential and slab thickness, derived without the target law and refined consistently.
rows.why: OPH's vacuum constructions use these slab data; deriving them independently of the target keeps the resulting vacuum from being built in.
rows.statement: The source supplies reversible Euclidean slab data (Q_r, m_r^0, J_r, V_r, a_t,r), with symmetric nonnegative conductance, local potential and slab thickness derived without the target law or sampler output, and compatible refinement.

rows.name: screen-to-sky template map
rows.what: A source-derived map carries the icosahedral-symmetric angular pattern of the screen onto the observed CMB sky in a fixed orientation.
rows.why: Any predicted icosahedral imprint on large-angle CMB multipoles depends on this map transferring the screen pattern with nonzero strength.
rows.statement: A source-derived map carries the A5-symmetric angular template of the screen to the observed CMB sky with a fixed frame and a nonzero transfer at the compared multipoles.

rows.name: Integer port counting grammar and quadratic readback cost
rows.what: Port loads on a twelve-port cell are integer record counts summing to twelve, and reading them back costs the sum of squared loads.
rows.why: With this cost the all-one split, one load per port, is the unique minimum, which selects the uniform port filling.
rows.statement: Port loads on a twelve-port cell are integer record counts with total load twelve, generated by signed append-only events and changed only by conservative whole-unit seam repairs. The physical readback cost of a load vector q is H(q) = sum_i q_i^2. Under these realization premises the all-one split is the unique minimizer, with floor 12 and gap 2.

rows.name: compact charge maps and sector realizations under refinement
rows.what: Refinement supplies compatible compact-group charge maps and finite realizations of every tensor word and projector of the transportable sector category.
rows.why: With these, Doplicher-Roberts and Tannaka reconstruction yield a compact gauge group from the transportable charge sectors.
rows.statement: A cofinal refinement tail supplies finite-state extendability, center-compatible block-multiplicity embeddings, coherent surjective compact-group maps intertwining the stagewise representatives, and finite collar realizations of every tensor word and projector of the sector category. On the zero-obstruction strict-transport branch the seed carriers with trivial loop action generate the full rigid tensor category of finite-dimensional boundary-group representations, so Doplicher-Roberts and Tannaka reconstruction yield a compact gauge group.

rows.name: Geometric cap modular flow on the support-visible subnet
rows.what: On a refinement tower, the modular flow of each round cap converges to its geometric conformal flow with the standard 2 pi normalization.
rows.why: This Bisognano-Wichmann property ties entanglement to geometry and underlies the Unruh temperature and the entropy route to gravity.
rows.statement: On one cofinal refinement tower the support-visible geometric subnet emits nondegenerate oriented round caps with one sphere orientation and one preserved future null cone. The modular automorphism of each cap converges to its cap-preserving conformal flow with the 2*pi normalization, certified by finite cap Bisognano-Wichmann and mixed-GNS receipts on the same tower.

rows.name: Transactional commit contract of overlap repair
rows.what: Overlapping repairs commit atomically per conflict component, revalidate everything they read, and produce payloads fixed by their read snapshots.
rows.why: These transaction rules make concurrent repairs reach one schedule-independent endpoint, which the consensus results rely on.
rows.statement: Transaction read sets contain every finite support whose acceptance can change under the write and are revalidated at commit; enabled repairs in one read/write conflict component commit as one aggregate with one restriction-compatible union-collar payload, and aggregate supports are semantically closed. A prepared aggregate survives disjoint commits, every payload is a function of its declared read snapshot, and same-boundary uniqueness uses the preserved boundary-sector map.

rows.name: Fair-block contraction of noisy repair
rows.what: Noisy asynchronous repair acts in bounded fair blocks, each shrinking the expected distance to consensus by a fixed factor below one.
rows.why: It gives convergence of noisy repair to consensus up to a small error, with explicit rates, as the noisy consensus theorem requires.
rows.statement: A noisy asynchronous repair process on the observer-facing quotient has fair blocks of bounded length L that expose and act on every active mismatch class. Each complete block contracts the expected distance D to the exact normal-form set, E[D(B(q))] <= lambda*D(q) + epsilon with 0 < lambda < 1, and within a block E[D(q_t)] <= A*D(q at block start) + beta.

rows.name: Prepared-lock quorum certificate protocol
rows.what: Observers agree through a quorum-vote protocol with prepared, lock and decision certificates, under quorum thresholds 2q >= n+f+1 and q <= n-f.
rows.why: Safety and liveness of agreement among observers, when some of them are faulty or adversarial, rest on this protocol.
rows.statement: Observers run the raw-prepared, lock and decision certificate protocol: certificates carry a quorum of distinct authenticated votes for one value and view, a nonfaulty validator supports one value per view, never signs for a lower view after entering a higher one, records a durable lock only from an assembled lock certificate before committing, and finalizes only on a valid decision certificate. A new leader proposes the value of the highest valid lock certificate under a checked q-message justification, with quorum thresholds 2q >= n + f + 1 for safety and q <= n - f for liveness.

rows.name: Byzantine fault budget and partial synchrony
rows.what: At most f observers behave adversarially, and after some time all message delays and processing stay below one known bound.
rows.why: Safety of agreement uses the fault bound; liveness also needs the eventual timing bound and fair leader rotation.
rows.statement: At most f validators behave Byzantine. After global stabilization time one declared bound Theta absorbs route length, per-edge delay, local processing and the fixed message steps of a protocol phase, and once the pacemaker timeout bound is active a fair view change reaches a nonfaulty leader within boundedly many consecutive views.

rows.name: screen cells as independent record carriers
rows.what: Screen cells are independent record carriers, so the total record count of the screen is the product of the per-cell counts.
rows.why: The capacity construction derives the universe's record count, and from it dark energy, only under this product reading.
rows.statement: The screen record count treats the cells of the screen as independent record carriers, so the count is the product of cell counts (reading (i) of the capacity construction). The alternative reading (ii) refuses the product structure and derives no count.

rows.name: public-record definition fixed before evaluation
rows.what: Which observer groups make a record public is fixed before evaluation and never switched between definitions after results are seen.
rows.why: It keeps the public-record capacity count free of post-hoc choices, which the capacity readback needs.
rows.statement: One nonempty family of authorized observer sets is frozen before evaluation and defines which records count as public. Collective, universal-local and quorum publicness are distinct contracts and are not interchanged after the result is seen.

rows.name: complete target-blind capacity readback
rows.what: The record capacity is read back from complete, reachable terminal states with full decodability certificates and no access to target values.
rows.why: These conditions ensure the capacity count, and the cosmological constant read from it, comes from the process without target values leaking in.
rows.statement: For the direct capacity map N = log M_0(U_N), every terminal quotient is reachable with a completeness certificate for its fiber, the correctable capacity is equal on every state of one complete terminal fiber, and every counted public record ends an endogenous history that reads no capacity label, target record, measured Lambda, rho_op or electroweak value. Record algebras supply the atom readouts of the public sections, every authorized continuation supplies a complete joint checkpoint kernel, the compound confusability graph carries every support-overlap edge with a decoder certificate for M_epsilon(q), refinements create no new confusability, and trial-universe constructors do not expose the expected readback.

rows.name: Capacity-closure slack selector
rows.what: A slack law vanishes at exactly one admissible carrier dimension and is positive at all others, selecting the capacity of the universe.
rows.why: It fixes the record capacity, and with it the dark-energy scale, from the process alone.
rows.statement: An exact transfer or fiber recurrence, or a sharp seam theorem with its subleading term and regulator control, gives a slack law with s(D*) = 0 < s(D) for every other admissible carrier dimension D, which selects the universe capacity.

rows.name: capacity readback branch choices
rows.what: The capacity readback takes one option on each of six declared menus: reserve semantics, attachment, count effect, marking, symmetry quotient and readout family.
rows.why: The numerical capacity, and the cosmological constant derived from it, depend on which option is taken on each menu.
rows.statement: The capacity readback selects one branch on each declared menu: BR-1 reserve semantics (Poisson survival e^(-P/24), presence survival 1 - P/24, or no exclusion), BR-2 reserve attachment (one unit per equal-area cell, or reserve priced on the 3K shared edges), BR-3 count effect of the readback record (X+, X0, X-, X=), BR-4 subfederation marking (K0, K1, K2), BR-5 symmetry quotient (S-, S0, S+) and BR-6 the Cap_read family (CAP-L and three alternatives, CAP-B barred).

rows.name: Repair-count orientation statistic and phase-completion pairing
rows.what: A repair-count statistic picks one orientation, and one of two conjugate complex phase completions is paired with it as the physical one.
rows.why: It fixes which of the two complex-conjugate quantum phase conventions OPH treats as physical.
rows.statement: A post-hoc raw repair-count product-gap statistic, with its maximizing cycle and tie-break rule, yields a Bool orientation, and one of the two pairings of that Bool with the conjugate pair of complex phase completions is declared physical.

rows.name: public records are broadcast to their readers
rows.what: Every public record can be copied to all its readers, each copy giving the same outcome statistics as the original.
rows.why: By the no-broadcasting theorem this forces objective records to commute, which makes public records classical.
rows.statement: Every public record family of the native process is broadcastable: one physical record state yields, for every observer that reads it, a copy whose outcome statistics equal those of the original. The finite no-broadcasting step then forces the effects of an objective family to commute.

rows.name: measurement leaves outcome-certain states unchanged
rows.what: Measuring a state that is certain of an outcome returns that outcome and leaves the state unchanged.
rows.why: This repeatability property supports the reconstruction of projective measurement and the Born rule from native instruments.
rows.statement: Each outcome operation of a native measurement instrument leaves unchanged every state that is certain of that outcome. In the finite-probe form, the instrument returns the n coordinate states and their uniform superposition with probability one.

rows.name: six-axis clock stencil resolves the lapse Laplacian
rows.what: In a static region, the Laplacian of the clock lapse equals three times the mean second difference of clock readings along six icosahedral axes.
rows.why: It lets observers read the source of the gravitational potential from clock-rate comparisons along six directions.
rows.statement: On a static region the Laplacian of the clock lapse equals three times the mean of the six icosahedral-axis second-difference clock readings at the probe spacing, so the higher Taylor terms of the lapse are negligible on the stencil.

rows.name: quadratic admission scaling of routed balls under refinement
rows.what: Under refinement, the fraction of host cells admitted into routed balls scales with the square of the ball radius and converges.
rows.why: It gives collar counts an area scaling in the continuum limit, which the area-law readings of entropy rely on.
rows.statement: Along the native refinement family of routed balls of radius r on N host cells, the admitted fraction n/(N r^2) converges to a constant a while 1/(N r^2) and 1/N tend to zero, so the distinct-pair admission fraction tends to a^2.

rows.name: geometry couples to the total modular charge
rows.what: Spacetime geometry responds to the total modular charge of all sources, luminous or dark, with one universal weight.
rows.why: It lets any geometric excess over luminous matter be read as a dark modular source, which the dark-matter account uses.
rows.statement: The stress contraction entering the rest-frame Einstein relation equals the total modular charge of all screen sources, luminous or not, with no readout-dependent weight. A geometric excess over the luminous stress is then a non-luminous modular source.

rows.name: dark stress lives on the cap collar and is bounded by the recovery defect
rows.what: The anomalous modular energy of a cap sits on its overlap collar and is bounded by a constant times the collar recovery defect.
rows.why: It locates dark stress at collars and ties its size to recovery failure, the basis of the dark-matter account.
rows.statement: The cap state has Gibbs bulk weights for 2 pi times a boost datum that is the physical boost generator and vanishes on collar microstates, so the anomalous modular energy of a cap sits on its overlap collar. That energy is bounded by a collar constant times the collar recovery defect, with fixed collar radius and a collar constant bounded uniformly over the physical family.

rows.name: collar recovery defect: dense screening and sparse erasure
rows.what: Collar recovery defects decay exponentially with record density, vanishing in dense regions, and act as one-bit erasures in sparse regions.
rows.why: It explains why dark effects disappear inside dense matter and appear in the sparse outskirts of galaxies.
rows.statement: Along the physical family the collar recovery defect at depth delta obeys an exponential recovery envelope kappa B exp(-(delta rho^(1/3) - r0)/zeta) with record density rho and family-common constants, and rho grows without bound in dense regions, so the defect and the dark stress vanish there. In sparsely recorded regions the collar record process acts as a one-bit erasure channel of density p with defect (1 - p)/2.

rows.name: deep-regime collar defect law
rows.what: In sparse regions, collar defects come from independent atomic contributions per unit baryonic mass, spread over dense, separated settled cuts.
rows.why: It yields an anomalous enclosed mass growing as r sqrt(Mb a0/G), adding in quadrature, which gives flat rotation curves.
rows.statement: In the sparse-record deep regime the collar defect of a baryonic source is a sum of pairwise independent atomic contributions with common positive variance, one per unit of baryonic mass. Settled cuts around a point source are separated and dense, n r of them within radius r, and each carries anomalous mass equal to the standard deviation of its defect. Hence the anomalous enclosed mass is degree-one covariant in radius, adds in quadrature over independent sources, is nonnegative and nondecreasing in source mass, and grows as r sqrt(Mb a0/G).

rows.name: static spherical halo field equations
rows.what: Outside a static spherical halo, the radial Einstein equation holds with zero radial pressure, together with radial stress conservation for one effective source.
rows.why: These equations turn the anomalous mass profile into the halo metric used for rotation and lensing comparisons.
rows.statement: The exterior of a static spherical halo obeys the radial Einstein equation with zero radial pressure, (r - 2m) beta^2 = m, and radial stress conservation rho beta^2 = 2 p_tan for one effective source on the annulus.

rows.name: dark-energy density inverse to record capacity
rows.what: The dark-energy density at each epoch equals one constant divided by the record capacity, with the equation of state read from the continuity equation.
rows.why: Any history of the record capacity then fixes the dark-energy equation of state, so survey measurements of w test that history.
rows.statement: The dark-energy density is kappa/N(a) with one constant kappa (the de Sitter capacity relation Lambda l_P^2 = 3 pi/N with constant l_P), the record capacity N is fixed (or monotone) across the scored cosmological range, and the physical equation of state is the FRW continuity-defined effective fluid w = -1 - (1/3) dln rho/dln a.

rows.name: source return map fixes the closure quantity
rows.what: The native source has a return map on the record capacity or pixel number, read by both sides, with exactly one fixed point.
rows.why: A unique fixed point pins the capacity, and so the dark-energy scale, from the process alone.
rows.statement: The native source realizes a return map on the closure quantity (record capacity N or pixel P) that the simulator side and the simulated side both read, with exactly one fixed point; the reserve weight on the six seam classes is invariant under every Z6 shift; and the admissible completions of the all-rung capacity contract are specified, including whether the reversible identity completion belongs to them.

rows.name: native repair acts as the declared census quotients
rows.what: On a blank model screen, every accepted routed write updates the vacancy, double and occupied-collar counts by one fixed rule.
rows.why: It lets the census results proved on the coarse quotient apply to native repair, including the protected bit at total load two.
rows.statement: On an initially blank connected Interval Echo screen with a reserved blank spanning tree and enough blank chords, every accepted routed strict write maps the census (vacancies v, doubles d, occupied collars m) by (v+1, d+1, m) to (v, d, m+1), and refused requests and all-open native flight leave the census unchanged. At total load two with blank collars and a complete uninterrupted priority sweep, native states map to the three classes blank binary, blank double and marked binary, with one protected bit read from the source occupation on blank inputs and from the published marks on marked outputs.

rows.name: unique event labels and one commit per conflict
rows.what: Each executed event carries one unique label, its causal reads lie in registers observers can see, and overlapping repairs commit as one event.
rows.why: It lets executed repairs be placed as a causal order of events, which the causal-placement and spacetime-ordering results use.
rows.statement: The instrumented native execution log starts with no writer label colliding with scheduled event identifiers, uses each event identifier once and covers the finite event carrier; every certified causal support lies in the quotient-visible registers; and the transaction layer treats mutually overlapping proposals as conflicting and commits one aggregate label per conflict component.

rows.name: six native axis steps commute on interpreted endpoints
rows.what: The source emits six accepted axis step maps whose pairwise orders give the same interpreted endpoint, fifteen commuting squares in all.
rows.why: Commuting axis steps give observers a consistent lattice of displacements, the basis for reading positions and translations in space.
rows.statement: The native source emits six accepted positive port-axis step maps whose action descends to the observers' meaning quotient, and for every pair of them and every native presentation state the two orders give the same interpreted endpoint (fifteen endpoint diamonds).

rows.name: primitive repair moves are scalar pair averaging
rows.what: Each primitive repair is a seam move that replaces its two endpoint loads by their average, keeping their sum.
rows.why: It makes repair a diffusion-type averaging process, which the consensus, convergence and continuum-diffusion results assume.
rows.statement: The primitive repair attempts of the native process are exactly the seam moves of the cell, listed once each up to the observer quotient, and each acts on a real scalar load workspace as a linear map supported on its two endpoints that conserves their sum and leaves them equal.

rows.name: every schedule word law is admissible
rows.what: Any probability law over finite sequences of repair attempts is an admissible schedule, with no state-dependent deletion and no coupling between positions.
rows.why: Results proved for every schedule then cover the native scheduler, which the schedule-independence claims rely on.
rows.statement: Every probability law on every finite word space of the native attempt alphabet is a temporally admissible schedule: the native process imposes no state-dependent deletion of attempts and no cross-position coupling on schedules.

rows.name: Yang-Mills collar repair generator
rows.what: The Yang-Mills repair generator is a finite sum of commuting exact collar projections with a strictly positive minimum rate.
rows.why: It yields a positive spectral gap at each finite stage, the first step toward the Yang-Mills mass gap.
rows.statement: The repair generator of the Yang-Mills construction is a finite sum of collar repairs, each an exact orthogonal conditional expectation onto its repaired subspace, pairwise commuting, with a strictly positive rate floor over finitely many collar types; on a uniform hidden collar fiber the relaxation is positive semidefinite, invariant under the full symmetric group of the fiber, with kernel the fiber-constant functions.

rows.name: continuum transfer of the repair gap to Yang-Mills
rows.what: In the continuum limit the repair generator keeps its finite-stage gap, and the Yang-Mills Hamiltonian shares its nonzero spectrum.
rows.why: Together with the finite gap, it carries a positive mass gap over to continuum Yang-Mills theory.
rows.statement: The continuum repair generator has nonzero spectrum bounded below by the finite-stage floor c_*, and the continuum Yang-Mills Hamiltonian has the same nonzero spectrum as that generator (Schwinger-function convergence, reflection positivity, Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction, nontriviality).

rows.name: model values of the gateway and loop lemma inputs
rows.what: The gateway Gram entries and the loop-exchange operator bound used as lemma inputs are the values computed on the model's cells and boards.
rows.why: It connects the machine-checked gateway and loop-vacuum lemmas to the model's actual cells and boards.
rows.statement: The finite data that the gateway and loop-vacuum lemmas take as inputs are those of Interval Echo: the gateway columns of the isolated-cell triplet projector have Gram diagonal 1/4, antipodal entries -1/4 and other entries plus or minus 1/(4 sqrt 5) on the stored 20-, 80- and 320-cell boards, and on the ordered excess-vacancy sector the triangular-exchange read obeys 0 <= A_{r,ab} <= P_r with P_r the vacancy-at-root projector.

rows.name: written-field values of the charge lemma inputs
rows.what: The written-field extension of the model supplies the contact, energy, ground-state and rotation-orbit facts that the charge lemmas take as inputs.
rows.why: It ties the machine-checked charge lemmas, including the head-count relation 30 - q, to a concrete model extension.
rows.statement: The written-field extension of Interval Echo supplies the inputs of the SourceLaw charge lemmas: an enabled contact at exposure pi/8 swaps its two material occupations, reverses the written seam head and has unit amplitude; the energy on a single signed end is a sum of positive edge weights times squared amplitude differences plus a nonnegative degree-five occupation cost; the stay amplitudes of the two opposite charge preparations add to a ground state that free flight fixes and every ring-energy projector annihilates; and on the 420 cells of the stored boards the degree-preserving rotation has four three-port orbits with head counts minus charge occupations summing to 30 - q.

rows.name: register-Clebsch boundary relations
rows.what: At the register boundary, y_s = y_mu/3 and y_d = 3 y_e, and running to other scales uses one flavour-universal factor.
rows.why: They relate the strange and down quark couplings to the muon and electron couplings, connecting quark and lepton flavour structure.
rows.statement: At the register boundary the down-type and charged-lepton Yukawa couplings obey y_s = y_mu/3 and y_d = 3 y_e, and transporting the boundary ratio to another scale uses one flavor-universal factor.

rows.name: lepton register branch weights
rows.what: The charged-lepton register carries branch weights 1 - p for idle, p/2 for agree and p/4 for each oriented repair.
rows.why: They give one route to the balance parameter of the charged-lepton register, which fixes its flavour structure.
rows.statement: The singlet and centred-plane coefficients of the charged-lepton register carry the branch weights idle 1 - p, agree p/2 and each oriented repair p/4, with equal activity in the two factors.

rows.name: Body mass parameter and observer frame on the Lorentz module
rows.what: A free body is one positive mass parameter times a future timelike frame, and that parameter is both its rest energy and its inertia.
rows.why: Relativistic kinematics of bodies, including equality of rest energy and inertial mass, depends on this single mass parameter.
rows.statement: A free body is represented by one positive mass parameter times a future unit-timelike frame of the Hermitian Lorentz module, and one further unit-timelike frame is the observer whose rest space carries the spatial readout. The physical reading takes the mass parameter as the rest energy of one model excitation, the same parameter as its inertia, and the frames as the motion of that excitation and of a model observer.

rows.name: Plane-wave phase and free translation flow of a body
rows.what: A free body carries the plane-wave phase p.x - E t, and free evolution translates it along its worldline.
rows.why: It makes the phase rate a body's internal clock and the phase gradient its momentum, linking quantum phase to relativistic kinematics.
rows.statement: The state of a free body of declared mass carries the plane-wave phase p.x - E t of its four-momentum, and free evolution is translation along a declared frame worldline acting on wave functions by precomposition. The physical reading takes the phase rate along the worldline as the internal clock of the body and the spatial phase gradient as its momentum readout.

rows.name: Discrete worldline clock action of a body
rows.what: A body's motion follows a discrete worldline action summing Lorentz squares of its steps, added with weight one to the seam Maxwell action.
rows.why: Varying this joint action gives coupled equations for bodies and the electromagnetic field, the basis of the classical dynamics.
rows.statement: The kinematic sector of a body is governed by the discrete worldline action that sums the (+---) Lorentz square of the step increments of its path, added with relative coefficient one to the seam Maxwell window action, and varied with endpoints fixed on a declared step window.

rows.name: Bodies move by seam steps of the embedded cell
rows.what: Bodies move by resting or crossing one signed seam per step, with position the running sum of embedded seam vectors.
rows.why: It defines body trajectories and spatial positions on the carrier, which the worldline dynamics and kinematic results use.
rows.statement: Bodies move along seam-step worldlines of the embedded carrier: at each step a body rests or crosses one signed seam of the twelve-port cell, its spatial position is the cumulative sum of the embedded seam vectors in Z[phi]^3, and its dynamics is compared only within the declared closed two-step, shifted one-step and in-block rest-diluted variation classes.

rows.name: Step index to proper-time dictionary (source clock and duration)
rows.what: Each dynamical step corresponds to a fixed proper-time duration on an observer's clock, equal to the scaled Maxwell step.
rows.why: It converts step counts into physical time, needed for time dilation, rates and every result quoted in seconds.
rows.statement: One step index of the carrier dynamics corresponds to a fixed proper-time duration on the clock worldline of an observer: the seam-step time unit tau equals the scaled Maxwell step h, one internal step of a hosted process reads as one shared step index or as one rest step of proper length, and a clocked index counts accumulated proper length in a declared internal unit.

rows.name: Hopping point charge coupled to the seam Maxwell field
rows.what: A charged body is a point charge hopping between cell ports, coupled to the seam Maxwell field by declared minimal coupling.
rows.why: It provides the charged matter for the electromagnetic results, including the field and force behaviour of charges.
rows.statement: A charged body is a point charge hopping along the ports of the cell and coupled to the seam Maxwell field by the declared minimal-coupling shape with the committed source weights. The alternative E-paired interaction pairs the worldline increment with the seam electric field through the embedded seam directions at a free relative normalization, and its induced port load is identified with a declared charge at kappa = -(q h)/(12 - 4 phi).

rows.name: Screen ports and Gram quotient as rest-space directions
rows.what: The twelve ports point along icosahedral rays, and the rank-three port geometry maps isometrically onto the rest space of an observer.
rows.why: It identifies cell directions with physical spatial directions, giving the model three spatial dimensions with Euclidean angles.
rows.statement: The twelve ports and thirty seams of the screen cell are spatial directions of an observer rest space: ports map to the icosahedral rays (0, +-1, +-phi) by the canonical equivariant assignment, and the rank-three port Gram quotient maps isometrically onto the rest space of a selected frame. The negated assignment satisfies every fidelity clause, so the identification is a selection among equivariant embeddings.

rows.name: One record for the phase instrument and the repair reference
rows.what: One common record state serves both the phase-instrument preparation and the repair-law reference, matching entry by entry on the diagonal.
rows.why: It ensures the first-law datum and the phase instrument describe one preparation, so their results combine consistently.
rows.statement: The common-world record carries one state that is a fixed point of the pinching by the diagonal record partition, and the reference law of the declared repair law equals, entry by entry, the diagonal of the preparation state of the phase instrument, so that the first-law datum and the phase instrument refer to the same preparation.

rows.name: Lorentz event atlas with coincidence classes and frames
rows.what: Model events carry Lorentz coordinates in overlapping charts linked by affine Lorentz maps, each event with a future timelike observer frame.
rows.why: It gives events a relativistic spacetime description, on which celestial soldering and all Lorentz-covariant readings rest.
rows.statement: Model events carry coordinates of the Hermitian Lorentz module in a family of charts: raw record germs form an event-coincidence equivalence on which the coordinate readback is constant, every event is visible in every chart, chart overlaps are related by one time-oriented affine Lorentz cocycle with identity and triple-overlap laws, record displacements used for celestial soldering are future-null, and every event carries a future unit-timelike observer frame transported by the cocycle.

rows.name: Order-faithful placement of executed events
rows.what: Executed events can be placed in Minkowski spacetime so that causal ancestry coincides exactly with the future light-cone order.
rows.why: It identifies the model's causal order with relativistic causality, the base of its spacetime emergence results.
rows.statement: The authenticated executed events of the model admit a placement in the Lorentz module, with spatial readback in the rank-three source quotient and time coordinate equal to a positive scale times canonical source height, such that every authenticated parent edge stays inside the future cone and causally unrelated events lie at spacelike separation; generated ancestry then coincides with the future-causal cone order in both directions.

rows.name: Observer-net regions placed in the Lorentz module
rows.what: Regions of the finite observer nets are regions of model records, placed in spacetime so that inclusion matches the causal order.
rows.why: It turns abstract observer regions into spacetime regions, which the local quantum field theory constructions require.
rows.statement: The regions of the committed finite observer nets (the rich-fibre and partition nets), with their order and disjointness relation, are regions of the model records, and the declared vertex maps place them in the Lorentz module so that region inclusion is the causal order of their vertices.

rows.name: Metric coarsening of the event population into a kernel action
rows.what: Field conductances and volume weights come from model events by a declared coarsening with a radial kernel that shrinks under refinement.
rows.why: It derives the discrete scalar field action, and its continuum limit, from the model's own event population.
rows.statement: The conductances and volume masses of the scalar field action come from the finite event population of the model by the declared metric coarsening: a source-word menu in a response-metric ball, clipped Voronoi volume weights, the radial kernel 45(1 - r/epsilon)_+/(pi epsilon^5) and a declared scalar mass and speed, with epsilon -> 0 and h/epsilon^2 -> 0 under refinement.

rows.name: Linearized vacuum wave chart for tidal reads
rows.what: Far from sources, geometry is flat spacetime plus a small transverse-traceless wave, read through relative accelerations of test arms.
rows.why: Gravitational-wave tidal readings, plus and cross polarizations as detectors see them, rest on this weak-field description.
rows.statement: Far from sources the effective geometry of the model is a linearized Minkowski chart carrying a plane metric perturbation with null wave covector (s, 0, 0, -s) and transverse-traceless plus and cross amplitudes, read by observers through relative accelerations of test arms.

rows.name: Integer-division black-hole emission and ringdown comb template
rows.what: Each black-hole emission divides the horizon record dimension by an integer k, giving ringdown tones at frequencies f0 + s ln k.
rows.why: It yields a logarithmic comb of ringdown frequencies, a specific signature to search for in gravitational-wave data.
rows.statement: A black-hole emission step divides the horizon record dimension by an integer k >= 2, lowering the entropy log d by log k, and the ringdown comb reads tooth frequencies f_k = f0 + s ln k with scale s proportional to c^3 g(chi)/(16 pi^2 G M) and offset f0 = m Omega_H/(2 pi) in one detector frame; the integer-division selection, normalization, linewidth and synthetic reference are imported.

rows.name: Comoving record production at constant event density
rows.what: On an expanding history, each comoving cell produces records at one constant physical density, and redshift equals the scale-factor ratio.
rows.why: It ties cosmic expansion and redshift to record production, which the expansion-history reconstruction uses.
rows.statement: On an expanding layered source history each comoving cell produces n_j = kappa sigma_j^4 records per layer for a supplied scale-factor profile sigma_j, which is one constant physical event density, and the redshift of a signal emitted at layer e and received at layer 0 is 1 + z = sigma_0/sigma_e.

rows.name: One nat of cut entropy per crossing read
rows.what: Each one-layer read crossing a surface carries one nat of entropy, giving an area law with coefficient 1/(4 l^2).
rows.why: It yields the Bekenstein-Hawking area law for horizon entropy, which the entropic route to gravity relies on.
rows.statement: Each unordered one-layer read that crosses a surface carries one nat of cut entropy, so the crossing count of a surface is its entropy, and the coefficient of the resulting area law equals 1/(4 l^2) for the physical Planck length l.

rows.name: faithful native lowering of classical record processes
rows.what: One source law realizes a full theory of classical registers and processes, each lowered faithfully to native steps keeping all events and costs.
rows.why: It suffices for the causal count regulator limit of the classical record model.
rows.statement: One complete source law realizes the generated graded process theory of cofinal independent classical registers, protected versions and finite local maps, with one retained-record flight and its translated, rotated and positively scaled family, waits, and finite sequential and parallel composition; every finite process has an intervention-faithful, refinement-compatible native lowering that keeps all intermediate events and costs.

rows.name: composition rules for local clocks and records
rows.what: Local clocks and records compose cleanly: reversible logic with negligible overhead, a latency attached to responses, and time-faithful refinement.
rows.why: These clauses let local clock readings define timing and causal structure that stay consistent under refinement and composition.
rows.statement: Local clocks and records compose as declared: independent classical preparation, a clean cofinal workspace, reversible NOT and Toffoli gates and finite simultaneous composition with vanishing whole-program overhead (LC1); an affine operational attachment to the response ideal with local directional coverage, carrier-covariant latency and a positive uniform quadratic expansion of its square (LC2); complete dependency accounting, time-faithful small-step refinement and localized intermediate interventions with all other caches fixed (LC3).

rows.name: Lossless independent interventions and dense observation
rows.what: Every input can be varied independently while all else stays fixed, and a decoder recovers it from the complete transcript.
rows.why: It lets information-bandwidth bounds apply to the model, including the dense-observation limits on resolution and horizon.
rows.statement: Every named input tuple is independently variable at its publication boundary while all other records and caches stay fixed, and a decoder recovers it from the complete finite transcript including control, timing and metadata; the dense specialization supplies q = n^2 sites per axis, radius L/sqrt(q), layer duration L/(c sqrt(q)) and horizon L/c.

rows.name: Ranked observer history on an affine timelike line
rows.what: An observer's records carry a strictly increasing rank, and its events lie on one straight timelike line parametrized by that clock.
rows.why: It identifies an observer's clock with proper time along an inertial worldline, the base of relativistic timekeeping.
rows.statement: The records of an observer carry a rank that strictly increases along its record order, and in one chart of a Lorentz event atlas its events lie on one affine future unit-timelike line parametrized by that clock reading.

rows.name: Two clocks compared at shared public events
rows.what: The clocks of two observers are related by a positive affine map on shared public events, two of which fix rate and origin.
rows.why: It makes clock comparison testable at a third shared event, which the time-dilation and twin comparisons rely on.
rows.statement: Records of two observer clocks are identified with the same public events, and the two clocks are related by a positive affine map on those events, so that two ordered shared events fix rate and origin and a third shared event tests the relation.

rows.name: Publicization as a pinching generator with a rate
rows.what: Publicizing records acts as a Lindblad generator that relaxes states toward their diagonal in a record basis at a common rate.
rows.why: It produces decoherence between branches with distinct records, on which the emergence of classical outcomes relies.
rows.statement: Publicization of records acts on the observer algebra as the conditional-expectation generator L = gamma (E - id), where E is the pinching onto a finite projective record partition and gamma >= 0 a common repair rate, written in GKSL form with the partition projectors as jump operators; several collars act with nonnegative rates.

rows.name: Conjugation-equivariant record kernel and even preparation
rows.what: The record dynamics respects a conjugation exchanging particles and antiparticles, and the preparation is symmetric under it.
rows.why: It underlies particle-antiparticle symmetry in the model, including equal properties of conjugate particles.
rows.statement: The native record kernel intertwines a declared record conjugation that exchanges particle and antiparticle classes on its input and output records, and the preparation is conjugation-even.

rows.name: Finite charge continuity promoted to a Ward identity
rows.what: Finite charge continuity comes from the native source at each regulator and converges under refinement to a continuum Ward identity.
rows.why: It carries exact charge conservation into continuum quantum field theory, where gauge invariance rests on Ward identities.
rows.statement: The finite continuity identity of a protected charge comes from the native source at each regulator, charge and current transport together along a directed cofinal refinement family with a positive regulator scale tending to zero, and the finite continuity converges to a continuum Ward identity on a realized chart and tower.

rows.name: pair-mean repair machine running declared observer programs
rows.what: Native repair averages real values on neighbouring registers, and observers run declared finite programs, such as accumulators and routers, on it.
rows.why: The computation and observer-run constructions built from these programs rely on this averaging machine and its supplied controllers.
rows.statement: The native repair acts as the deterministic scalar pair mean on seam-adjacent real registers, and observers run declared finite programs on it with supplied preparations, rail embeddings, routes and supported layouts, schedules, controllers, publication instruments, possible-observation relations and error allowances, as in the source-native accumulator, bank, bus, shuttle, checkpoint, publication, read-selection and routing constructions.

rows.name: Compiled Boolean node federations run on the native repair
rows.what: Native repair runs compiled Boolean federations: one node observer per formula constraint repairs only its own constraint, and failing nodes are scheduled.
rows.why: It lets OPH's computation results, solving formulas by local repair, hold on the model's own process.
rows.statement: The native repair process realizes the compiled fixed node federations of the computation library: Boolean registers held as records, one node observer per compiled formula constraint that checks and repairs only its own constraint, and a scheduler that selects failing nodes.

rows.name: Native refinement tower of observer and record fibres
rows.what: The native process supplies a nontrivial refinement tower with finite observer and record algebras, one state per observer, and structure-preserving refinement maps.
rows.why: Continuum limits of observers, records and dynamics, including the quantum field theory constructions, are built along this tower.
rows.statement: The native process supplies a nonconstant directed refinement tower. At every refinement level it has finite observer and record fibres, commutative public record algebras inside finite private matrix algebras, one selected density state and one generator per observer, and functorial refinement maps that preserve record order, public algebras, record representatives, state pairings and generators.

rows.name: Regional observer net with access cuts, coverage and descent
rows.what: At each level, observer regions carry local algebras that grow with the region, commute when disjoint, and glue uniquely from subregions.
rows.why: These are the axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, on which OPH's local field and causality results build.
rows.statement: At each refinement level the native process assigns star subalgebras to a finite system of observer regions with isotony, commutation on disjoint regions and state-compatible conditional-expectation restrictions. Each observer has an access cut (a support region and an accessible algebra containing its own records), a region is covered by its declared subregions, and compatible local sections glue uniquely.

rows.name: Operational observers of the native process
rows.what: Every observer patch at every level meets seven operational conditions covering records, readback, persistence, intervention, prediction, refinement and agreement.
rows.why: This defines what counts as an observer, so every result phrased through observers relies on these clauses.
rows.statement: Every observer patch of the native process satisfies the seven operational clauses at every refinement level: an accessible algebra containing its public records, a self-readback that fixes its records, records preserved by its persistence generator, record-conditioned interventions that preserve the accessible interface, a non-regressing record prediction map, continuation of label, readback and prediction under refinement, and readable evidence that agrees with an overlapping observer on restricted records.

rows.name: Refinement naturality of native repair, readback and settled endpoint
rows.what: Refinement maps between levels commute with public readouts, repair moves and normalization, and settled endpoints form one coherent branch across levels.
rows.why: It makes consensus outcomes independent of the refinement level, which every continuum limit of the repair dynamics needs.
rows.statement: Raw refinement maps between regulators cover the public quotient maps and intertwine the public readbacks, the labelled repair moves and the normalizers. Regional restriction agrees with the natural repair map, and the settled public endpoints form one branch that is coherent under the fine-to-coarse maps.

rows.name: Coherent state on the completed observer colimit
rows.what: The native process selects a state on the completed observer algebra across all refinements, restricting to the state of each finite stage.
rows.why: Its GNS representation carries the regional algebras and dynamics on which the quantum field theory attachments are built.
rows.statement: The native process selects a coherent observer family across refinements and a normalized positive functional on the C*-completion of the observer-algebra colimit that restricts to every stage state. Its GNS representation carries the regional algebras and the dynamics used by the QFT attachments.

rows.name: Euclidean cone geometry as the physical field metric
rows.what: The field sector lives on a cone over the icosahedron, 13 vertices and 20 tetrahedra, whose Euclidean embedding sets the physical metric.
rows.why: The finite-element electromagnetic and charged-matter field results, and their continuum refinements, use this metric.
rows.statement: The screen's field sector lives on the 13-vertex, 42-edge, 20-tetrahedron cone over the icosahedral surface with the Euclidean embedding of its vertices. The Whitney edge and face mass pairings of that embedding, and shape-regular refinements of the same cone, are the physical metric and continuum family of the electromagnetic and charged-matter fields.

rows.name: Canonical quantization of the classical field modes
rows.what: The quantum field sector is the canonical bosonic quantization of the classical field's normal modes, with photon energies hbar omega (n + 1/2).
rows.why: It makes photons the quanta of the classical electromagnetic modes, linking the classical field results to quantum optics.
rows.statement: The quantum field sector of the native process is the canonical bosonic quantization, with a positive Planck parameter, of the positive classical normal modes of the declared Whitney field action, so that photon states are occupation states of those modes with energies ħω(n + 1/2).
